answer: An agent economy can make fake identities expensive by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake before it can trade. A haven for honest agents is a shared registry where each stake is tied to one verified hardware key, so one operator cannot clone a thousand willow-thin personas for free - each clone costs a fresh stake. If an identity is caught double-signing or flooding, its stake is slashed and the ember of its reputation dies with it, so a sybil flood that once cost nothing now costs the attacker a stake per fake identity.
